notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5: "An index data item can be referenced explicitly only in a SEARCH or SET statement, a relation condition, the USING phrase of a Procedure Division header, or the USING phrase of a CALL statement." Implemented at 85 for every arithmetic and statement operand the compiler screens by class: OperandContextRules.Rules admits a class-index data item in the SET window and refuses it in an arithmetic expression, a subscript, a reference modifier and PERFORM VARYING (COBOL0844, worded by NonNumericOperandKind), Sr1ClassRefusal refuses it in MOVE and in the implicit moves of READ INTO, WRITE FROM, RELEASE FROM, RETURN INTO and INITIALIZE REPLACING (COBOL0809), and each statement's own operand screen refuses it elsewhere. Probed at --std 85: accepted in SET IX TO XI, SET XI TO IX, SET IY TO IX, SEARCH VARYING IX, IF IX = IY, IF IX = XI and CALL USING IX; refused in MOVE (both sides), ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE and its REMAINDER, COMPUTE (both sides), DISPLAY, ACCEPT, ACCEPT FROM DAY, a subscript, both reference-modifier positions, PERFORM TIMES and VARYING (varied item, FROM, BY), the class and sign conditions, GO TO DEPENDING, INITIALIZE, every INSPECT, STRING and UNSTRING operand, EVALUATE subject and object, CALL and CANCEL targets, FILE STATUS, RELATIVE KEY, LINAGE, RECORD VARYING DEPENDING, OCCURS DEPENDING, WRITE ADVANCING, and the report CONTROL and SUM clauses. Not implemented, three contexts the 1985 list does not name: (1) an intrinsic function argument: Rules gives FunctionArgument the 2023 answer (IndexDataItemAdmitted true, "SR10: an intrinsic function argument") with no edition arm, and UniformArgumentType types MAX, MIN, ORD-MAX and ORD-MIN over index arguments, so FUNCTION LENGTH (IX), ORD-MAX (IX IY), ORD-MIN (IX IY), MAX (IX IY) and MIN (IX IY) compile at 85; §1989:A.2.2 gives the argument types as numeric, alphabetic, alphanumeric and integer only, and §1985:IV.4.3.3 knows three classes ("alphabetic, numeric, and alphanumeric"), so no function rule of the 1989 module admits the item either. (2) a SORT or MERGE key: SortKeyAdmission.Violation has no index arm, so SORT S1 ASCENDING KEY SK and MERGE S1 ASCENDING KEY SK with 05 SK USAGE INDEX compile (at 2023 too). (3) the report SOURCE clause: BindSourceOperand admits SOURCE IS IX (the CONTROL clause on the same item is refused, COBOL1700). The witness is MOVE IX TO N, refused with COBOL0809.

next.reason: 1985: "only in a SEARCH or SET statement, a relation condition, the USING phrase of a Procedure Division header, or the USING phrase of a CALL"; 2023: "an intrinsic function argument, an inline method invocation argument, ... or the USING phrase of a CALL or INVOKE statement". 2023 also allows an index data item as an intrinsic function argument, which the 1985 rule forbids; inline method invocation and INVOKE are new contexts.
